plainName: Care of a dependant with disability
summary: If you are resident and spent money on the medical treatment, nursing, training and rehabilitation of a dependant with disability, or paid into an approved scheme for their maintenance, a deduction is allowed, larger where the disability is severe. A dependant is your spouse, child, parent, brother or sister who depends wholly or mainly on you. Under the new Act the deduction is up to the limit, so never more than you spent or paid; under the earlier Act it was the limit itself once anything was spent or paid. Only the old regime allows it.

disqualifiers.description: It is not deducted in the default regime.
A dependant who claims the deduction for their own disability is not a dependant for this one.
Support for more than one dependant with disability in the year is not computed.
